Francis Bacon on knowledge

Francis Bacon (1561–1626) approaches knowledge within empiricism. He catalogued idols that distort judgment and advocated gradual induction from observations and experiments. Systematically, the teaching links induction, science, method into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets knowledge most directly—useful for searches such as “francis bacon quotes on knowledge.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the Francis Bacon thinker page for biography and to the knowledge theme for other voices on the same question.
